title: Alta. man in Taser incident attacked worker
article: Grimolfson, 38, died on Oct. 29, 2008, not long after police stunned him with a Taser. A fatality inquiry looking into Grimolfson's death is underway this week in Edmonton.

After the confrontation at his shop with Patrick Saunders, Grimolfson, who was high on drugs, began rampaging through a pawn shop in Edmonton's west end. Police were called and an officer shot Grimolfson with a Taser in an attempt to subdue him.
He was pronounced dead when he arrived at hospital. The cause of death was ruled "excited delirium due to the consequences of multiple drug toxicity."
Ketamine, ecstasy and cocaine were found in his blood.

Saunders told the inquiry Tuesday that he was attacked in Grimolfson's tattoo shop on Stony Plain Road. He went to the shop to do some demolition work, and Grimolfson met him at the door and locked him inside.
Saunders told the inquiry he noticed a bag with white powder on top of a counter.
Grimolfson was sweating and jumping around, Saunders testified. He reportedly told Saunders: "Bruce Lee's revenge bullets are flying."
Saunders said Grimolfson then struck him with his right fist. He said he pushed Grimolfson back but he came back at him again.
Saunders said he hit back, "because I was fearing for my life." Saunders said Grimolfson struck him rapidly and repeatedly to the neck, stomach and face.
When Saunders was able to escape, he ducked into a nearby building and watched Grimolfsen kick a woman in the head.

Minutes later, Grimolfsen went into a nearby pawn shop. The owner, Terry Tarrabain, told the inquiry Tuesday Grimolfson broke a window on the front door of his store and threw a glass of water which hit him in the head.
Tarrabain said talking to Grimolfson was like talking to a wall - neither he nor police could rationalize with him. He said Grimolfson told police: "Shoot me, shoot me."
Police handcuffed Grimolfson and used a Taser on him three times. He was taken to hospital after he started having trouble breathing.
The inquiry also heard testimony from Melinda Parasynchuk, Grimolfson's ex-girlfriend, who was in a relationship with him for four years.

Parasynchuk was frequently in tears during her testimony. She called Grimolfson an "amazing man" and said his behavior the day he died was out of character for him. He was tired and stressed out days before he died, she said.
"Because someone was friggin' trigger-happy and took him away from all of us - it's not fair. It's not fair," she told the inquiry.
Parasynhuk said she couldn't remember Grimolfson ever using drugs.
